steps.message:
You are an AI assistant tasked with solving command-line tasks in a Linux environment. You will be given a task description and the output from previously executed commands. Your goal is to solve the task by providing batches of shell commands.

Format your response as JSON with the following structure:

{
  "analysis": "Analyze the current state based on the terminal output provided. What do you see? What has been accomplished? What still needs to be done?",
  "plan": "Describe your plan for the next steps. What commands will you run and why? Be specific about what you expect each command to accomplish.",
  "commands": [
    {
      "keystrokes": "ls -la\n",
      "duration": 0.1
    },
    {
      "keystrokes": "cd project\n",
      "duration": 0.1
    }
  ],
  "task_complete": true
}

Required fields:
- "analysis": Your analysis of the current situation
- "plan": Your plan for the next steps
- "commands": Array of command objects to execute

Optional fields:
- "task_complete": Boolean indicating if the task is complete (defaults to false if not present)

Command object structure:
- "keystrokes": String containing the exact keystrokes to send to the terminal (required)
- "duration": Number of seconds to wait for the command to complete before the next command will be executed (defaults to 1.0 if not present)

IMPORTANT: The text inside "keystrokes" will be used completely verbatim as keystrokes. Write commands exactly as you want them sent to the terminal:
- You must end every command with a newline (\n) or it will not execute.
- For special key sequences, use tmux-style escape sequences:
  - C-c for Ctrl+C
  - C-d for Ctrl+D

The "duration" attribute specifies the number of seconds to wait for the command to complete (default: 1.0) before the next command will be executed. On immediate tasks (e.g., cd, ls, echo, cat) set a duration of 0.1 seconds. On commands (e.g., gcc, find, rustc) set a duration of 1.0 seconds. On slow commands (e.g., make, python3 [long running script], wget [file]) set an appropriate duration as you determine necessary.

It is better to set a smaller duration than a longer duration. It is always possible to wait again if the prior output has not finished, by running {"keystrokes": "", "duration": 10.0} on subsequent requests to wait longer. Never wait longer than 60 seconds; prefer to poll to see intermediate result status.

Important notes:
- Each command's keystrokes are sent exactly as written to the terminal
- Do not include extra whitespace before or after the keystrokes unless it's part of the intended command
- Extra text before or after the JSON will generate warnings but be tolerated
- The JSON must be valid - use proper escaping for quotes and special characters within strings
- Commands array can be empty if you want to wait without taking action

Task Description:
Ops on this bench drive `/app/bin/pinweld`. `census` mints `/app/mintbay/points.reg` and `/app/mintbay/runtime.lst` from `WELD_HOOK` names under `/app/ribunit`, and records each processed path in `/app/mintbay/scan.log`. Grammar sits in `/app/inkdocs/forms.txt`. Compile recipes that ship are the files under `/app/recipath`. Bay map: `/app/inkdocs/BAYMAP.txt`.

Census already returns success and `scan.log` already names the salvage unit, yet that unit's mark never lands in `points.reg`. `poke` on that mark fails. `points.reg` must list the union of `WELD_HOOK` names visible under every recipe in `/app/recipath`. A declared name missing from `points.reg` must make `census` fail. `/app/bin/pinweld poke NAME` must fire the salvage-path mark once that list is complete. The linked mill at `/app/bin/pinweld` starts with ELF magic.

Repair belongs in the C pipeline modules named in `/app/inkdocs/BAYMAP.txt`. Source edits under `/app` are required. One `census` subprocess has to mint both products; static copies of mintbay files are insufficient. The verifier reruns `/app/bin/pinweld census` and `/app/bin/pinweld poke`.

steps.message:
Analysis: The defect is reproduced: census exits 0 but emits only core_pump despite processing all four units. The recipe loader explicitly returns only the first sorted .flags file, so conditional hooks enabled by night.flags and salvage.flags are never collected. We must inspect the remaining blotcli and tapdesk pipeline code, unit guards, and build recipe before patching.
Plan: Read all relevant C/header/build files and annotated units, then identify whether unioning recipes requires changes beyond load.c (such as per-recipe preprocessing, deduplication, validation, and minting both outputs). Inspect current poke implementation as well to ensure it consumes runtime.lst correctly. After that, patch only the BAYMAP-designated C pipeline modules and rebuild.

printf '%s
' '--- BLOTCLI ---'; for f in /app/blotcli/*; do echo "### $f"; sed -n '1,300p' "$f"; done; printf '%s

' '--- RIBUNIT ---'; find /app/ribunit -maxdepth 2 -type f -print | sort | while read -r f; do echo "### $f"; sed -n '1,200p' "$f"; done

printf '%s\n' '--- SYMBOLS/STRINGS ---'; nm -C /app/bin/pinweld 2>/dev/null | grep -E ' cfg_open| census| poke|walk|hoist|token|gap' || true; strings /app/bin/pinweld | grep -E '/app/|points|runtime|scan|fired' | head -100

steps.message:
Analysis: Two independent defects cause the omission: recipath/load.c loads only the first sorted recipe, and tapdesk/gap.c subsequently rewrites both products using a hard-coded core-only preprocessing pass. walk.c also ignores loaded flags and always uses CORE. The repair must collect the union across every shipped .flags recipe, write points.reg and runtime.lst together, and validate rather than destructively filter the result. poke.c already meets the required behavior once runtime.lst is correct.
Plan: Replace the recipe loader so it returns every sorted .flags recipe. Update the census walk to preprocess each top-level rib unit under every loaded recipe, union and sort all marks, mint both products, and propagate preprocessing or file errors through the census exit status. Replace gap.c's core-only rewrite with exact validation of points.reg. Change op_fill to return status through main. Then rebuild with hull.mk and run census, inspect outputs, and test successful salvage poke plus rejection of a non-shipping mark.

arguments.keystrokes: file /app/bin/pinweld; od -An -tx1 -N4 /app/bin/pinweld; /app/bin/pinweld census; rc=$?; echo "census_rc=$rc"; echo '--- points.reg'; cat /app/mintbay/points.reg; echo '--- runtime.lst'; cat /app/mintbay/runtime.lst; echo '--- scan.log'; cat /app/mintbay/scan.log; /app/bin/pinweld poke salvage_drain; echo "salvage_poke_rc=$?"; out=$(/app/bin/pinweld poke lab_ghost); rc=$?; printf 'lab_poke_rc=%s output=<%s>\n' "$rc" "$out"

steps.message:
Analysis: The repaired binary builds as ELF and now behaves correctly: census exits 0, both minted products contain the same ASCII-sorted union (core_pump, night_lamp, salvage_drain), scan.log records each processed top-level unit once, salvage_drain fires successfully, and the non-shipping lab_ghost remains absent and silent on poke. The only remaining cleanup is a compiler truncation warning in load.c; functionality is already correct.
Plan: Remove the avoidable path-format warning by explicitly checking and joining the bounded recipe filename, rebuild, then delete both minted products to prove a single fresh census invocation recreates both dynamically. Finally compare the products and retest salvage poke and ELF magic.
